strings.title: PIN_TUMBLER
strings.subtitle: Problem: phone numbers in many formats
strings.briefing:
The contact list was typed by forty different people. Phone numbers show up as (415) 555-0132, 415.555.0132, +1 415 555 0132 and a dozen other shapes.

The lock opens for exactly one shape: 415-555-0132. Strip everything that is not a digit, keep the last ten, then put the dashes back.

Regular expressions do the heavy lifting here. In pandas use .str.replace(..., regex=True). In SQL use the built-in helper REGEXP_REPLACE(text, pattern, replacement), which takes $1-style group references.

df is loaded. 150 rows, 4 columns.
strings.task: Phone numbers are written in many different styles. Rewrite every phone number as 415-555-0132: three digits, a dash, three digits, a dash, then four digits.

starterCode.python:
# df is loaded. 150 rows, 4 columns.
# Look at the phone column first.
df['phone'].head(15)

python: Remove every non-digit first: df['phone'].str.replace(r'\D', '', regex=True)
Keep the last ten digits with .str[-10:] so a leading country code disappears.
Then insert dashes: .str.replace(r'(\d{3})(\d{3})(\d{4})', r'\1-\2-\3', regex=True), and assign it back to df['phone'].
sql: Keep the last ten characters with SUBSTR(value, -10).
Insert dashes: REGEXP_REPLACE(value, '^(\d{3})(\d{3})(\d{4})$', '$1-$2-$3'), wrapped in UPDATE data SET phone = ...
